ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, ABCD is a square, D is at the upper left, C is at the lower left, A is at the upper right, and B is at the lower right; point E is located on the right side of the square, triangle ABE is constructed outward from the square with AB as a side, and the figure also connects D to E. Reasoning: Because ABCD is a square, AD = AB, and ∠DAB = 90°. Because ABE is an equilateral triangle, AB = AE, and ∠BAE = 60°. From AD = AB and AB = AE, AD = AE is obtained, therefore triangle ADE is an isosceles triangle. Also because E is outside the square, ray AE is located in the outside direction of AB, so ∠DAE = ∠DAB + ∠BAE = 90° + 60° = 150°. In isosceles triangle ADE, the base angles ∠AED and ∠ADE are equal, therefore ∠AED = (180° - 150°) / 2 = 15°.

raw_record.question_text: In the adjoining figure, $ABCD$ is a square, $ABE$ is an equilateral triangle and point $E$ is outside square $ABCD$. What is the measure of $\measuredangle AED$ in degrees?

method.method_draft: Synthetic isosceles-triangle route. First read from the image that A is the upper-right vertex of the square, D is upper-left, B is lower-right, and E lies to the right so that triangle ABE is attached externally along side AB. From the text, use that ABCD is a square and ABE is equilateral. Since AD = AB in the square and AB = AE in the equilateral triangle, AD = AE, so triangle ADE is isosceles. At A, the angle between AD and AB is 90 degrees, and the angle between AB and AE is 60 degrees; because E is outside the square as shown, these combine to give angle DAE = 90 + 60 = 150 degrees. Therefore the two base angles of isosceles triangle ADE are equal, so angle AED = (180 - 150)/2 = 15 degrees.

method.method_draft: Coordinate/trigonometric route. Read from the image that AB is vertical, AD is horizontal to the left, and the equilateral triangle ABE is built to the right of AB. From the text, assign the common side length as 1. Place B = (0,0), A = (0,1), D = (-1,1). Since ABE is equilateral outside the square on the right, E = (sqrt(3)/2, 1/2). Then vector EA = (-sqrt(3)/2, 1/2), whose direction is 150 degrees from the positive x-axis. Vector ED = (-1 - sqrt(3)/2, 1/2), so its direction is 180 degrees minus arctan((1/2)/(1 + sqrt(3)/2)) = 180 degrees minus arctan(1/(2 + sqrt(3))). Since 1/(2 + sqrt(3)) = 2 - sqrt(3) = tan 15 degrees, ED has direction 165 degrees. Thus angle AED is 165 - 150 = 15 degrees.
